description:
Found while baking the pebble-packing artwork (crates/outram-park-fork-liggghts/examples/bake_pebble_packing.rs, 2026-08-06).

DemSimulation carries no accumulated tangential spring displacement between steps (documented in simulation.rs 'Honest scope'), so the tangential force is a Coulomb-capped dashpot only. Consequence: there is NO STATIC FRICTION. A grain resting on an inclined contact always creeps at a small terminal velocity, and a settled bed can never reach a strict zero-velocity rest state.

Measured evidence from the bake (2525 spheres, 74000 steps, dt=1e-4 s, dynamic-relaxation quench with the velocity field zeroed every 200 steps):
  - creep over two back-to-back 0.50 s windows: rms 4.18 % then 3.72 % of a pebble radius; max 16.6 % then 20.2 %. Steady, not decaying -> a floor, not an unfinished transient.
  - local solid fraction over the same windows: 0.6069, 0.6101, 0.6112 -> the packing STRUCTURE is stable even though grains keep creeping.
  - ensemble kinetic energy likewise floors out (~3e-1 J for 2525 pebbles) because the quench removes momentum that gravity immediately restores.

Fix: add per-contact tangential history state (the accumulated spring displacement xi_t, keyed by particle pair and carried across steps) so a resting contact can sustain a static tangential force. That also unlocks angle-of-repose verification, which is the standard DEM validation case for friction and is currently impossible.

Also worth having once that lands: a cone/frustum Boundary variant. The bake had to approximate the conical vessel bottom with 32 inscribed flat Wall half-spaces.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
MAINTAINER'S CALL, 2026-08-06: not a blocker, and not to be treated stringently for artwork purposes.

The packing baked in crates/outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/components/pebble_packing.rs is ARTWORK. Its structure is settled — solid fraction stable at 0.6069 / 0.6101 / 0.6112 across measurement windows, against ~0.61 for a real pebble bed — and that is the only property the drawing depends on. The residual creep (rms ~4% of a pebble radius, steady rather than decaying) does not affect how it looks.

So: DO NOT re-run, re-settle, post-process or otherwise chase equilibrium for the sake of the widgets. Use the bake as-is.

This bead stays open because the underlying limitation is REAL and would matter if the DEM is ever used for physics rather than pictures: simulation.rs's tangential contact is history-free (a Coulomb-capped dashpot with no accumulated tangential spring), so there is no static friction and a grain on an inclined contact creeps indefinitely. Strict rest is unreachable. That is worth fixing when someone wants granular DEM results, not before.

Dropped to reflect that it gates nothing currently in flight. The honest caveat in the module doc STAYS — documenting the limitation costs nothing and prevents the packing being cited later as a settled-equilibrium result. Documenting it is not the same as being stringent about it.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
MAINTAINER'S DECISION, 2026-08-12: keep the DEM bake for the vessel artwork. 'some creep is okay.'

Context — a third packing option arrived on develop today: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/crp_packing.rs, a Jodrey-Tory close-random-packing generator measured at 0.5796 realized packing fraction (N = 1107). The three now coexist:

  RSA (sphere_packing.rs)      ~0.38 ceiling   too loose for a pebble bed
  Jodrey-Tory (crp_packing.rs) 0.5796 measured  fills a domain to a target fraction
  DEM bake (pebble_packing.rs) 0.6112 measured  gravity-settled in the real barrel+cone

The DEM bake stays because it is both DENSER and more PHYSICAL for this purpose: it settles under gravity into the actual vessel geometry, which is what makes the bed rest on the cone and taper into the chute. Jodrey-Tory has no gravity, so it would not reproduce that structure — it is the better tool for TRANSPORT geometry, where a target fraction in a simple domain is what you want.

So: do not swap the artwork to CRP, and do not re-run the DEM chasing equilibrium. This bead stays open only for the underlying engine limitation (history-free tangential contact, no static friction), which matters if the DEM is ever used for granular physics rather than pictures.

title: DEM: history-free tangential contact prevents a true static packing

description: score_collision uses the collision estimator only; add a track-length estimator over free-flight segments. MacroXs has no absorption column so ScoreType::Absorption is approximated as (Sigma_t - Sigma_s)/Sigma_t; add real Sigma_a.
title: outram-mc: track-length tally estimator + explicit Sigma_a column on MacroXs

description: Issue #30 comment 2026-08-22 03:05 UTC: 'I also want pdf reader to be able to view images like okular as well.' Today PdfReaderState (src/digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs) only accepts a PdfDocument via kopitiam_pdf::mupdf; there is no path for a plain PNG/JPG. Needs: PdfReaderState (or a new enum wrapping it) to hold either a rasterized PDF page or a directly-loaded PlotRaster/ColorImage, dispatched via an enum per the workspace's no-trait-objects rule, so the same pan/zoom/scroll viewer in pdf_reader.rs serves both. The file dialog's filter set (Images + PDF) already exists (op-689u) -- this is about the *viewer*, not the picker.
title: kovan-gui: PDF reader should view raster images (PNG/JPG) directly, Okular-style
